Death is something everyone should fear to a degree. When I thought about it I realized I was afraid of death but with that fear came a new form of respect. Without fearing and respecting death, you can never truly live, or atleast in my opinion. Death is the most powerful force to ever exist, and that is what I fear about it, the sheer brutal strength it has over everything else in this world.

I don't know. I feel like one cannot really live unless one loses some of their fear over death. People these days are so terrified over the smallest of things that they don't bother to enjoy themselves. They keep their children on a leash, they don't take up many hobbies that is deemed risky, and they cower to people trampling over their way of life simply because they are so accustomed to avoiding death at all costs.

What I am trying to say is that I don't want to die, but if I do, I want to die as a consequence of actually living my life the way I want to live it. I fear being an old man regretting my cowardice more than suffering an early death.

That's why I fear but respect death, there is no escaping it and we have to embrace that and continue in life.

My best assessment of the truth is that there is nothing after death. If I'm wrong I may end up in a great deal of pain, if you believe some of the religious types, but I'd rather believe my best assessment of the truth as I am able to understand it than believe something for which there is no genuine evidence. I may end up in Hell, but if an honest search for the truth is what gets me there, it's a price I'm prepared to pay.
